input_schema.description: Assemble the most relevant memory context for a query. Use this tool to retrieve stored facts before answering or planning. Do not use this tool to ingest new content. Arguments are a flat snake_case object with `query`, `fact_types`, legacy `as_of`, independent `valid_at` and `known_at` timestamps, optional exact `known_revision`, `budget`, `view_mode`, `window_start`, and `window_end`. `as_of` cannot be combined with the new temporal fields; `known_at` and `known_revision` are mutually exclusive. Historical reads return snapshot and completeness metadata and can be partial while revision-unsafe selectors are withheld. For an empty partial result, follow its guidance: it may permit one query refinement. To preserve the exact snapshot, copy `context.snapshot.valid_at` to `valid_at` and `context.snapshot.known_revision` to `known_revision`; omit `as_of` and `known_at`, and leave other selectors unchanged. An empty retry does not establish absence or make a partial snapshot complete. Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. Retry validation errors only after correcting the invalid arguments; do not blindly repeat other failed calls.

as_of.description: The timestamp to assemble context as-of (ISO 8601 format, default: now)

budget.description: Maximum number of facts to return (default: 5)

compact.description:
Request compact (token-efficient) response. Defaults to true.
Set to false for verbose debug output including full rationale strings.

fact_types.description: Optional fact types to include in the response

known_at.description: Server-knowledge boundary (ISO 8601), resolved to a committed revision.

known_revision.description: Exact committed knowledge revision; mutually exclusive with known_at.

query.description: The query to assemble context for

valid_at.description: Valid-time boundary (ISO 8601), independent of server knowledge time.

window_end.description: Optional upper bound for result timestamps (ISO 8601 format)

window_start.description: Optional lower bound for result timestamps (ISO 8601 format)

input_schema.description: Extract entities, facts, and relationships from remembered content. Use this tool when you need structured knowledge from an existing episode or from new inline content. Prefer task-based invocation when the client supports MCP Tasks or when local NER may exceed the client's synchronous timeout. Do not use this tool for retrieval. Arguments must be a flat snake_case object. Provide exactly one input source: `episode_id` for stored content, or inline `content`/`text`; optional fields are `source_type`, `source_id`, `t_ref`, `zero_shot_labels`, and `include_fact_evidence` (defaults to true; set false for a compact response). Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. If you pass inline content, the server ingests it first and then extracts facts. Complete statement/quote pairs are included only within a 4 KiB serialized evidence budget; if any pair is unavailable or the budget is exceeded, all evidence pairs are omitted and `fact_evidence_omitted` is true.

content.description: Content to analyze (optional if episode_id provided)

include_fact_evidence.description:

callers can set this to false to request the compact response.

zero_shot_labels.description: Custom zero-shot entity labels for GLiNER (opt-in, overrides default labels)
